baseline: work/A10 (direction A Optimus-lean, best after 3 rounds)
note: Evidence abridged by the author from the critic's full report; verdicts and preference verbatim.
reads_as_reason: The head is a rounded block on almost no neck, the shoulders are huge and the arms flare, the torso is a slab with a dished pelvis, and the legs are untapered tubes.

G1.evidence: Block head on a wide shoulder shelf; neck nearly invisible (P2a 0.1103); P3 0.418, arms read as wings; legs straight tubes (P8a 0.9375, P8b 0.9705).

G2.evidence: Chest slab with a ledge at the black waist band, pelvis a separate dished shape; thigh and shank parallel cylinders, no calf swell near the top (P9b 0.4467). Black bands read as deliberate recesses; the shapes between them do not flow.

G3.evidence: Matte warm-white shells, graphite bands, gloss black visor, no accent; bands uniform on arms and legs.

G4.evidence: Arm, leg and head shells share one soft rounded-box language, but the backpack and black heel blocks are sharp boxes; chest and pelvis squareness differ from the soft limbs; S4b 0.5141.

G6.evidence: S2 IoU 0.5248 / 0.5566. Matches head, hip and knee heights and white-over-graphite. Not: shoulder width, wide A-pose, no neck, untapered legs, long foot (P10a 0.238).

pairwise.evidence: Silhouettes near-identical; B3's bands are uniform and complete, chest and back clean. A10 has irregular black blotches on the shoulder and forearm in the 3/4 view and a black slab on the shoulder in the side view that look like unfinished masking. A10's leg taper (P8a) and P5 are slightly better.

top_changes.change: Narrow the shoulders, slim the upper arm and bring the arms in.
Visible neck; chest tapering into the waist and a pelvis that is not a separate dish.
Taper thigh and shank; shorten the foot.

notes: Facet banding in the clay render hides surface continuity; A-pose arms inflate the front silhouette.
